LESSON: WATER CONSERVATION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Matter
Topic 2.3: Water Conservation

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

Music Hallo learner, welcome to a Science and technology lesson for Grade 4 learners. Today we are going to learn about factors that affect floating and sinking. Have the following items with you, a basin half filled with water, a normal flat bottle top, a crushed bottle top, a piece of wood, a piece of metal and a short pencil or a long pencil. Your radio teacher is Dominic Muhia. Welcome to the programme. Music

SECTION 2: TEACHING CONTENT

Music Hallo learner, welcome to a Science and technology lesson for Grade 4 learners. Today we are going to learn about factors that affect floating and sinking. Have the following items with you, a basin half filled with water, a normal flat bottle top, a crushed bottle top, a piece of wood, a piece of metal and a short pencil or a long pencil. Your radio teacher is Dominic Muhia. Welcome to the programme. Music

Hallo learner, welcome to Science and Technology lesson for Grade 4. Today we are going to learn about factors that affect floating and sinking. We are going to talk about factors that affect floating and sinking. Learner, before we begin I want you to get a basin that is half filled with water and the following solids: get a basin half filled with water and the following solids: two bottle tops, a normal flat bottle top and a crushed bottle top . Two bottle tops, one a normal flat one and the other bottle top I want you to crush it get also a piece of wood and a piece of metal just a small piece of wood and a small piece of metal, then a short pencil and a long pencil. Music Welcome back learner before we begin I want you to tell me what is Matter? What is matter? Music Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space. Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space. We have three states of matter. They are solids, liquids and gases. The three states of matter include solids, liquids and gases. Learner, what is the difference between floating and sinking? We have looked at different solids that float and sink in water, what is the difference between floating and sinking? Music The objects that remain at the surface of water are floating. The objects that remain at the surface of water are floating. While those that go to the bottom of the water are sinking. Those solids that go to the bottom of the water are sinking. Materials that sink are called sinkers while the materials that float are called floaters. Can you name examples of solids that float on water? Learner, name two floaters. Music Solids that float on water or those that remain on the surface of the water include a paper, a pencil, a leaf and many others. A paper, a pencil and a leaf are called floaters because they float on water. Now name the solids that sink in water. Learner name two sinkers. Music Solids that sink in water include stone, key, coin and many others, and therefore a stone, a key and a coin are called sinkers because they sink or they go at the bottom of the water. Learner, have you asked yourself why some object sink while others float on water? Why do we have sinkers and floaters? Objects float or sink according to a number of reasons. These reasons are known as factors. Today I want us to look at the factors or the reasons that affect floating and sinking. I want us to look at the factors or reasons that affect floating and sinking. Do you have your basin that is half filled with water? And the solids, the two bottle tops?

A flat one and a crushed one, a piece of wood and a piece of metal, together with a short and long pencil? We want to see this factors that affect floating and sinking. Music Let us put together the two bottle tops in the basin that is half filled with water. Remember one bottle top is normal, it is flat while the one is crushed. Learner, what do you notice? Music The normal flat bottle top floats on water while the crushed bottle top sinks in water. What did we do to the bottle top to make it sink? Music Learner, all this are bottle tops but one is floating while the other one is sinking. What did we do to the bottle top to make it sink? We crushed the bottle top and it sunk in water. A normal bottle top floats on water. Once we changed its shape it sunk in water. Therefore, shape is one of the factors or reasons that affect floating and sinking. We have different solids that float or sink in water. However, once we change their shape, then it will affect their floating or sinking. Once we change their shape it will affect their floating or sinking. Look at a ship, a ship is made of metal or steel. Do metals float or sink in water? Music Metals sink in water but a ship floats on water. Metals sink in water but a ship floats on water. Learner, can you tell me why a ship floats on water? Music A ship floats on water because it has a hollow shape. Once again shape is a factor that affects floating and sinking. Metals sink in water but a ship which is made of metal floats on water this is because it has a hollow shape. Now let us try and put the piece of wood and the piece of metal in water, which one floats and which one sinks? Music A piece of wood floats on water while a piece of metal sinks in water. What makes a piece of wood float on water yet a metal sinks in water ? Is it the shape? Music

Did you say Shape? No it is not the shape. There is another factor or reason that affects floating and sinking of an item . The answer is material . The material is the reason why a piece of wood floated in water while a piece of metal sank in water. The type of material affects floating and sinking. The type of material affects floating and sinking. Materials such as paper and wood floats on water while those made of metal and steel sink in water. Therefore, material is another factor that affects floating and sinking. Now finally let us get the short and the long pencil. Let us put the short and the long pencil in water. Music Which one floats and which one sinks? Answer when you hear the music . Music I hope you have put the two pencils in water. What have you realised? Music Both pencils float on water. A short pencil and a long pencil float on water. Learner, which factor of floating and sinking were we looking at ? Music When we test a short and a long pencil, we are looking at their size. The size of a material DOES NOT affect floating and sinking. The size of a material DOES NOT affect floating and sinking. We have now seen three factors or reasons that affect floating and sinking. Now learner name three reasons that affect floating and sinking. Do that when the music begins. Music Good. I hope you were able to answer. I have said the following reasons will affect floating and sinking: The shape The material and The size. When you change a shape of an object, it will affect whether the object will sink or float. Size will not affect a material, whether short or long if it sinks then it sinks and if it floats then it floats. However, the type of material will make the object to float or sink in water. For your task or activity at home, find other factors that affect floating and sinking. With that learner, we have come to the end of our Science and Technology lesson for today. Goodbye.

Music That has been a Science and Technology lesson for Grade 4 learners. In the program, your Radio teacher was Dominic Muhia. Let us put in the solids and we place them one by one and record whether they are floating or sinking. Do that when the music begins. Music Learner. Now say the objects that sink and float on water from your observation. Name the floaters and the sinkers that you have observed. Music Solids that float on water include: pen, paper, leaf and rubber. A pen, a paper, a leaf and a rubber are known as floaters, this is because they float or they remain at the surface of the water. Solids that sink in water include glass, stone, coin and key. A glass, stone, coin and a key are called sinkers. They are sinkers because they sink or they remain at the bottom of the water. Different solids float or sink on water. A short pencil floats, A long pencil also floats, I know why! The size of the material. Music Learner, the poem is about sinkers and floaters. Learner, what are floaters? Music From the poem, we hear that the type and shape of the material affects whether an item floats or sinks. The type and shape of the material affects whether an item floats or sinks. A plasticine ball sinks while a plasticine boat floats . Learner, which factor makes the plasticine ball to sink and the plasticine boat to float? Answer when you hear the music. Music

The factor is the shape. The material is the same, that is, plasticine. The material is the same, that is, plasticine. But the different shapes made from the plasticine affects floating and sinking. Music A coin sinks while a leaf floats. Again we hear from the poem a coin sinks while a leaf floats. The shape of a coin is different from that of a leaf . Learner, looking at a leaf and a coin which factor affecting floating and sinking do we notice? Is it the shape or the material. Music A coin sinks while a leaf floats because of the type of the material. Even though a coin and a leaf do not have the same shape the material is different. Remember the materials that sink are called sinkers while those that float are called floaters, and the type of material always affects floating and sinking. The type of material always affect floating and sinking. Different materials float while different materials sink, if you look at a ship, a ship floats on water because it has a hollow shape. Shape is a factor affecting floating and sinking. A piece of wood floats on water while a piece of metal sinks in water. The type of material affects floating and sinking. A short pencil and a long pencil float on water whether it is short or it is long it doesn’t affect. Size will not affect floating and sinking. I want us to find out this question, can floaters be made to sink? can floaters be made to sink? Music Yes floaters can be made to sink, by adding more weight to the floater. From the poem, a plasticine boat is a floater because it floats. If we add some weight to the boat, like we add coins or stones, the plasticine boat will sink. Therefore adding more weight to the floater will make the floater to sink. Music Learner, name an example of a floater and how you can make it a sinker. Name an example of a floater and how you can make it a sinker . Music A pencil floats on water but when you tie it to a stone it will sink. When you tie a floater to a heavy object, then the floater will sink. Floaters can be made to sink by adding weight on them. Even a ship which floats on water if you overload it then it will sink. We can therefore make floaters to sink and the main way of making floaters to sink is by adding more weight to the floater. Music This is your homework. F ind other floaters that can be made to sink. Show your parents or guardians when you are done. And with that learner we have come to the end of our Science and Technology lesson for today.
